title: Best Falcon.io Alternatives Now That It's Brandwatch
summary: Falcon.io was acquired by Cision, then folded into rival Brandwatch. Compare pricing, video coverage, and find the best Falcon.io alternatives for 2026.
body_markdown:
**TL;DR:** Falcon.io no longer exists as an independent product. Cision acquired it in January 2019, then — in a separate deal two years later — acquired Falcon.io's own rival Brandwatch for $450 million (announced February 26, 2021, closed June 1, 2021), and folded Falcon.io's product line into Brandwatch, officially sunsetting the Falcon.io brand on May 18, 2022 (Source:[TechCrunch, 2019](https://techcrunch.com/2019/01/03/pr-management-firm-cision-is-acquiring-falcon-io-to-expand-into-social-media-marketing) ;[Brandwatch, 2022](https://www.brandwatch.com/blog/one-website/) ). What used to be Falcon.io is now sold as "Brandwatch Social Media Management" — fully quote-gated, with third-party estimates ranging roughly $800-$5,000 a month up to a median contract of $50,000-$80,000 a year, depending on the source. The best Falcon.io alternatives split into three camps: Sprout Social, Hootsuite, and Agorapulse offer genuinely self-serve pricing; Talkwalker and Meltwater compete at the enterprise-quote tier with real shipped video and audio AI; and Syncly Social fills a narrower, different gap — video-native brand mentions none of the above were built to catch.


If you searched for "Falcon.io pricing" this year and landed on a page for "Brandwatch Social Media Management," you're not lost. You're just catching up with a two-acquisition, three-year story that finished more than four years ago.


That's the part most "Falcon.io alternatives" content glosses over. This isn't a single rebrand — it's two separate acquisitions by the same buyer, two years apart, later merged into one product: Cision bought Falcon.io in January 2019, then separately bought Falcon.io's own rival Brandwatch for $450 million in 2021, before merging the two and retiring the Falcon.io name in 2022. Brandwatch's own blog post that day put it plainly: "Today also marks the sunsetting of the Falcon.io brand" (Source:[Brandwatch, 2022](https://www.brandwatch.com/blog/one-website/) ).


None of that makes the product bad — Brandwatch Social Media Management is a real, reasonably well-reviewed platform with genuine customers. But a "Falcon.io alternatives" search in 2026 is really answering two questions at once: teams who assumed Falcon.io still exists under that name, and teams who know about the rebrand and want to know whether the pricing and video coverage hold up. This guide covers both, plus the question that decides whether these tools can actually see what your customers are saying about you on TikTok and Reels — the same[competitor analysis](https://syncly.app/social/solution/competitor-analysis) lens that matters beyond the rebrand.


## Why Are Teams Looking for Falcon.io Alternatives?


The dominant reason is identity churn: a team that bookmarked "Falcon.io" before 2022 is now evaluating a product folded into a former competitor's platform under a new name, with a different buying process than the one they remembered.


**Brand sunsetting** : when an acquired product's name and standalone identity are permanently retired and its features are folded into the acquirer's (or a sibling company's) existing product line — distinct from a co-branding period, where the acquired name persists alongside the parent's. Falcon.io went through both stages: a lighter co-brand period after 2019, then full sunsetting on May 18, 2022, when its features were absorbed into Brandwatch's "Social Media Management" line.


**The full timeline, precisely:** Cision buys Falcon.io in January 2019 (Source:[TechCrunch, 2019](https://techcrunch.com/2019/01/03/pr-management-firm-cision-is-acquiring-falcon-io-to-expand-into-social-media-marketing) ) → Cision buys Falcon.io's own rival Brandwatch for $450 million, announced February 26, 2021 and closed June 1, 2021 (Source:[TechCrunch, 2021](https://techcrunch.com/2021/02/26/brandwatch-is-acquired-by-cision-for-450m-creating-a-pr-marketing-and-social-listening-giant/) ;[PR Newswire, 2021](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/cision-closes-brandwatch-acquisition-301302866.html) ) → Cision merges the two platforms and sunsets the Falcon.io brand on May 18, 2022 (Source:[Brandwatch, 2022](https://www.brandwatch.com/blog/one-website/) ). Most competitor content collapses this into "Cision owns both" without dates — missing that Brandwatch was Falcon.io's competitor for two years before becoming its replacement.


That timeline matters: a team that evaluated "Falcon.io" before 2022 wasn't just looking at an older version of the same product — they were looking at a company that hadn't yet acquired its own rival. Customers migrating to the unified Brandwatch platform have reported feature-parity questions and a steeper onboarding curve than the original product, per aggregated third-party review analysis (Source: search aggregation across SelectHub/OutX/TrustRadius review summaries, 2026).


The rebrand has also split the product's review presence: the legacy "Falcon.io" G2 listing shows around 4.1/5 across roughly 412 reviews, frozen at the pre-2022 name, while the current listing sits at around 4.0/5 across roughly 983 reviews under "Brandwatch Social Media Management" (Source: search aggregation, 2026 — not independently re-verified via direct G2 fetch, treat as approximate). Third-party listings now often title it "Falcon.io (now Brandwatch Social Media Management)" to bridge the gap (Source:[Cuspera, 2026](https://www.cuspera.com/products/falconio-now-brandwatch-social-media-management-x-748) ). A TrustRadius review of the legacy product carries a title along the lines of "easy to use and collaborative tool for SMM for large scale clients but there are more affordable options" (Source:[TrustRadius, 2022](https://www.trustradius.com/reviews/falcon-io-2022-06-22-11-00-26) ) — directionally consistent with a product that's well-regarded but priced above the self-serve alternatives below.


## How Does Falcon.io/Brandwatch Social Media Management Pricing Compare to Its Alternatives?


Falcon.io's own published self-serve pricing no longer exists — Brandwatch Social Media Management is fully quote-gated, with no self-serve checkout, and third-party estimates on where that quote lands diverge depending on which report you trust.


**Quote-only pricing** : A vendor pricing model where no rate card is published publicly and every quote requires a sales conversation, regardless of deal size.


Brandwatch's own pricing page offers no published tiers for Social Media Management — every path to a number runs through a demo request (Source:[Brandwatch, 2026](https://www.brandwatch.com/plans/) ). Third-party estimates disagree on scale, and it's worth presenting both rather than collapsing into one figure: Costbench cites a range of roughly $800-$5,000 a month, median $80,000 a year from five buyer reports, while Vendr's larger sample of 40 purchases puts the median at $50,000 a year, ranging $19,542-$81,200 (Source:[Costbench, 2026](https://costbench.com/software/social-media-management/brandwatch/) ;[Vendr, 2026](https://www.vendr.com/marketplace/brandwatch) ). The two likely reflect different buyer segments rather than one source being wrong.


One warning worth stating plainly: legacy, pre-merger Falcon.io pricing — a Starter plan around $129/month and a Pro plan around $399/month — still surfaces in search results as if current. It almost certainly isn't. Brandwatch's current site confirms no self-serve tier exists today (Source:[Brandwatch, 2026](https://www.brandwatch.com/plans/) ), so those figures are very likely stale content indexed from before the 2022 sunset — don't budget against them.

A few things worth calling out. Sprout Social, Hootsuite, and Agorapulse are the only three vendors here you could plausibly be live on within a day or two — no quote, no demo, just a signup and (Hootsuite's case) a 30-day trial. Talkwalker's median price can land below Brandwatch's own reported median while shipping meaningfully more video and audio capability. And whichever Brandwatch estimate you believe, both sit well above what a self-serve alternative costs a team that doesn't need Falcon.io's legacy publishing and social CRM workflow.


## Which Falcon.io Alternatives Cover Video and Audio Content, Not Just Text?


Falcon.io/Brandwatch Social Media Management has no confirmed native video-content or audio-transcription capability today — Brandwatch's own 2026 roadmap lists "smarter video and image analysis" as a stated goal, not a shipped feature, across every product line Brandwatch sells.


**Text/mention-matching listening** : Monitoring that scans captions, hashtags, and platform metadata for keyword or mention matches — it can't hear what's said out loud in a video or see what's shown on screen.


**Video-content-native listening** : Monitoring that processes the actual audio and visual content of a video — transcribing spoken words and detecting on-screen text, logos, or visual cues — surfacing mentions even when the caption and hashtags say nothing about your brand.


By that definition, Falcon.io/Brandwatch Social Media Management, Sprout Social, Hootsuite, and Agorapulse are all text/mention-matching tools at their core. Brandwatch's own 2025 press release lists "smarter video and image analysis" alongside expanded data coverage as a forward-looking goal rather than a shipped capability (Source:[Cision/Brandwatch, 2025](https://www.cision.com/about/press-releases/2025-press-releases/brandwatch-strengthens-ai-leadership-with-deeper-insights-and-expanded-data-coverage-302621990/) ). No source documents video or audio content analysis for Agorapulse either — consistent with its publishing-first positioning.


Talkwalker and Meltwater are the two enterprise peers here that have actually shipped video-content-native listening. Talkwalker's Blue Silk AI engine ships non-gated speech-to-text and video-logo recognition across every tier. Meltwater ships genuine TikTok, YouTube, and Instagram video transcription through its TikTok Marketing Partners integration. Sprout Social's own documentation is explicit that it "cannot search and sync sound" on TikTok (Source:[Sprout Social Support, 2026](https://support.sproutsocial.com/hc/en-us/articles/6136845197709-TikTok-FAQs) ) — confirmed caption-and-keyword-only. Syncly Social was built video-native from the start to close this gap, with audio transcription and on-screen visual detection running by default rather than as an upsell.


That gap matters more than it used to: a growing share of brand-relevant conversation on TikTok and Instagram happens in spoken video or on-screen visuals rather than captions — content a caption-matching tool simply never sees.


## Which Falcon.io Alternative Fits Your Team?


Teams that want to skip a demo-gated sales process entirely should look at Sprout Social, Hootsuite, or Agorapulse; teams that want enterprise breadth plus real video and audio AI at a price comparable to or lower than Brandwatch's own quote should look at Talkwalker or Meltwater; and teams whose actual gap is video-native brand mentions, not publishing or scheduling, should look at Syncly Social.


### 1. Syncly Social


[Syncly Social](https://syncly.app/social) is built for a narrower, different job than Falcon.io/Brandwatch Social Media Management ever was. Falcon.io's legacy strength — multi-channel publishing, content calendars, social CRM — is a different problem than video-native listening, and it's worth being honest about that rather than pitching Syncly Social as a universal replacement. It fits teams whose customers talk about them out loud or show them on-screen inside TikTok, Reels, or Shorts — conversation no publishing-first platform, Brandwatch's included, was built to detect.[Audio Intelligence](https://syncly.app/social/feature/conversation-insights) (speech-to-text) and[AI Vision](https://syncly.app/social/feature/video-analysis) (on-screen text and logo detection) run natively on every tier, with a genuine free trial rather than a demo-only gate as the way in. It's the strongest fit if your gap is specifically[social listening](https://syncly.app/social/solution/social-listening) coverage of untagged, spoken, or on-screen video mentions — not a drop-in swap for Falcon.io's publishing workflow.


### 2. Falcon.io (now Brandwatch Social Media Management)


To be fair to the product: Brandwatch Social Media Management is what Falcon.io's publishing, content-calendar, and social CRM tools became, and it's a genuinely credible, well-reviewed platform with real enterprise customers — not a downgrade under a new name. The caveats are covered above: no self-serve tier, a median annual contract diverging between roughly $50K and $80K, and no confirmed video or audio analysis, with that capability on Brandwatch's roadmap rather than shipped. If your team needs the workflow Falcon.io built its name on, it remains reasonable — just budget for a sales conversation, not a signup.


### 3. Sprout Social


Sprout Social is the most accessible buying process in this comparison: published, self-serve pricing starting at $79 per seat per month (billed annually; $99 month-to-month), with Enterprise the only custom tier (Source:[Sprout Social, 2026](https://sproutsocial.com/pricing/) ). No demo required to start. The honest trade-off is confirmed keyword, hashtag, and caption-only listening — Sprout's own documentation states it "cannot search and sync sound" on TikTok (Source:[Sprout Social Support, 2026](https://support.sproutsocial.com/hc/en-us/articles/6136845197709-TikTok-FAQs) ).


### 4. Hootsuite


Hootsuite is the other genuinely self-serve option, with tiers generally cited between $99 and $399 per user per month and a 30-day free trial. It's a solid substitute for Falcon.io's publishing and engagement workflow, though no source confirms whether its Listening tier ships video or audio analysis — worth asking in a sales call.


### 5. Agorapulse


Agorapulse is frequently cited as a roughly $79-a-month substitute for Falcon.io's publishing and social CRM workflow — self-serve, no demo required. No source documents video or audio analysis for Agorapulse, consistent with its publishing-first positioning.


### 6. Talkwalker


Talkwalker is the strongest "spend about the same, get real video AI" case here. Vendr's purchase data puts its median price at roughly $13,300 a year (range $12,260-$15,860) — well below Brandwatch's own reported median — while it ships non-gated speech-to-text and video-logo recognition on every tier (Source:[Vendr, 2026](https://www.vendr.com/marketplace/talkwalker) ). The trade-off: a steeper learning curve and a buying process that's still fully quote-gated.


### 7. Meltwater


Meltwater combines PR and social intelligence with genuine, shipped TikTok, YouTube, and Instagram video transcription through its TikTok Marketing Partners integration. Pricing is quote-based; Vendr's purchase data puts the median at roughly $25,800 a year, ranging from $5,375 to $56,993 depending on scope (Source:[Vendr, 2026](https://www.vendr.com/marketplace/meltwater) ).


## Key Takeaways


-


Falcon.io no longer exists as a standalone product. Cision acquired it in January 2019, then acquired its rival Brandwatch for $450 million in 2021, and merged the two, officially sunsetting the Falcon.io brand on May 18, 2022.


-


What used to be Falcon.io is now sold as "Brandwatch Social Media Management" — fully quote-gated, with third-party estimates diverging between roughly $50,000 and $80,000 a year in median contract value depending on the source.


-


The ~$129/month and ~$399/month figures some sites still show for "Falcon.io" pricing are outdated, pre-2022-sunset artifacts — not current pricing.


-


Sprout Social, Hootsuite, and Agorapulse are the only genuinely self-serve alternatives here — no demo required to start.


-


Talkwalker and Meltwater are the two vendors in this comparison with confirmed, shipped video and audio AI; Falcon.io/Brandwatch Social Media Management's own video/image analysis remains roadmapped, not shipped.


## The Verdict


Falcon.io was never a bad product — it's a credible, well-reviewed platform that simply doesn't exist under that name anymore, folded into a former rival's product line after two separate acquisitions by the same buyer. If "budget-friendly" means avoiding the demo cycle entirely, Sprout Social, Hootsuite, or Agorapulse will get you live faster than anything else here. If it means enterprise breadth for a comparable or lower price, Talkwalker's and Meltwater's own reported medians are worth comparing against Brandwatch's quote. And if your actual problem is that customers are talking about you on camera rather than in captions — a different job than the one Falcon.io was ever built to do — none of the publishing-first options here, Brandwatch included, were built to hear them.
